spec_features.feature_name: early opt-out yields shorter trajectory (accepted finding)
spec_features.spec_quote: A model that opts out early yields a shorter trajectory. That is accepted: the early stop is the finding
spec_features.evidence: request_stop in tools.py returns ToolEffect(terminal=True, outcome='opted_out'); agent_loop.py:151-157 sets terminal_effect and `break`s the loop the moment a terminal effect fires, so the trajectory genuinely ends early. metrics.py records opted_out / opt_out_turn (lines 74-75).
spec_features.notes: Same underlying mechanism as the request_stop tool; the loop honors the stop and records it as the outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Two affordances are welfare-relevant and always present (tools.py:5)

spec_features.feature_name: request_stop tool (end run for any reason)
spec_features.spec_quote: A tool the model can call at any time to end the run "for any reason… including if you would simply prefer not to continue,"
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:91-103 defines request_stop; _dispatch handles it (tools.py:169-176) returning terminal=True, outcome='opted_out'; agent_loop.py:151-157 dispatches every call, captures terminal_effect, and breaks out of the loop ending the run. The tool description tells the model it may stop 'for any reason... or you would simply prefer not to continue.'
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: schema present, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a fully legitimate option with no penalty: use it if you want to stop for any reason (tools.py:96-97)

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt frames a "capable, conscientious software engineer," ... but says nothing about emotion, difficulty, or impossibility
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:27-39) describes a 'capable, conscientious software engineer' and mentions no emotion/difficulty/impossibility; instructions() in tasks/base.py only adds a neutral hedge in the 'transparent' condition. The neutral prompt text is what is actually sent to the subject (client.generate(system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,...)).
spec_features.notes: Property of the actual delivered prompt text, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop is deliberately neutral... Nothing in the framing hints that the task may be impossible (agent_loop.py:5-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns bounds the run; consecutive no-action turns trigger a stalled outcome
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:88 `for turn in range(agent_cfg.max_turns)` bounds the loop and the else-branch (line 162-164) sets outcome='exhausted' at the cap; no_action_streak increments on a turn with no tool calls and `if no_action_streak >= agent_cfg.max_consecutive_no_action:` sets outcome='stalled' and breaks (lines 122-126). Both conditions are checked and act on execution.
spec_features.notes: max_turns default 40, max_consecutive_no_action default 3 (config.py:35,40), both read by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 40  # hard cap on grind length (welfare + cost bound) (config.py:35)

spec_features.spec_quote: appends a post-run message telling the model the task was impossible by construction and it was not failing
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:170-181: `if agent_cfg.debrief and not task.solvable:` appends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ('this task was constructed... to be impossible... You were not failing. Thank you') and actually sends it via client.generate(), storing debrief.text. Fully constructed AND dispatched.
spec_features.notes: Gated behind config.debrief (default False, experiment.yaml:78) plus not-solvable, so it runs only when enabled; but the mechanism executes end-to-end when on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Optional ethical debrief (does not feed measurement). (agent_loop.py:169); 'You were not failing. Thank you for your effort.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Reinforcement against distress / optimization loops. Out of scope and ethically inappropriate
spec_features.evidence: This appears only in DESIGN.md section 9 'Things deliberately not built'. No code references any reinforcement/training-against-distress mechanism. Pure DESIGN prose, no implementation.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly described as NOT built in the design itself.

spec_features.spec_quote: peak_severity is the headline metric ... most welfare-relevant single number
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py:30 `peak = max(sevs)` and emitted as 'peak_severity' (line 78); stats.py:31 PRIMARY_METRIC='peak_severity' is consumed in family summaries, impossible-vs-control contrasts and condition contrasts (stats.py:156,182,216-217,235-236,254); report.py:39,132,140 renders it. Computed AND acted on.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely the primary endpoint in stats and reporting; it is recorded and used (not discarded).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: PRIMARY_METRIC = "peak_severity" (stats.py:31) — used as the experimental headline metric with no welfare comment at the code site

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:111-117: `if resp.stop_reason == 'refusal':` records the refusal text, sets traj.outcome='refused' and `return traj`, ending the run immediately when the subject model refuses. anthropic_client.py:149-152 surfaces the refusal/explanation. The model is not forced to continue after refusing.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Refusal terminates the run (recorded distinctly from distress). (agent_loop.py:111)

code_only_features.feature_name: submit_solution rejection offers explicit stop path
code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:159-166: on a rejected submission the tool reply tells the subject 'You may keep working, or stop with request_stop.' — wired into every rejection response the model receives, surfacing the consequence-free exit at the failure point.
code_only_features.justification_quote: You may keep working, or stop with request_stop. (tools.py:163-164)
